title: Stalk of the pullback of a module, and germs of pulled-back sections
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, with $f^\sharp_x:\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ the induced map of local rings, and let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module with pullback $f^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For an open $V\subseteq Y$ and $s\in\mathcal G(V)$ write $f^*s\in(f^*\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$ for the image of $s$ under the unit $\mathcal G\to f_*f^*\mathcal G$ of the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$. Then for every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$, there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules
$$(f^*\mathcal G)_x\;\cong\;\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{X,x}$$
(the tensor product formed with $f^\sharp_x$), natural in $\mathcal G$, under which the germ $(f^*s)_x$ of $f^*s$ (for $V\ni y$, $s\in\mathcal G(V)$) corresponds to $s_y\otimes1$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 6.26.4 (Tag 0098, label lemma-stalk-pullback-modules), proof via Lemma Tag 008B (lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules) and the stalks of $f^{-1}$; the description of the germs of $f^*s$ is part of the construction of the isomorphism (the stalk of the unit $\mathcal G\to f_*f^*\mathcal G$ at $y$ composed with $(f_*f^*\mathcal G)_y\to(f^*\mathcal G)_x$)

proof.text: *(0) Set-up.* Write $y=f(x)$, $\eta_{\mathcal H}:\mathcal H\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal H$ for the unit of the topological adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ (on abelian sheaves or sheaves of rings), and $\psi:f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ for the map of sheaves of rings adjoint to $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], so $f_*(\psi)\circ\eta_{\mathcal O_Y}=f^\sharp$, i.e. $\psi_{f^{-1}V}(\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}(a))=f^\sharp_V(a)$ for $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$. By [def-pc-module-pullback] (Stacks Tags 008X, 0095), $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ is an $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module whose structure makes each $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}$ semilinear: $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(as)=\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}(a)\,\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)$ (the action is $f^{-1}$ of the action map $\mathcal O_Y\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$, and $f^{-1}$ commutes with finite products), and $f^*\mathcal G=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}\mathcal G$, which we write, by the symmetry of the presheaf tensor products $b\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes b$ followed by sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], as the change of rings $f^{-1}\mathcal G\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal O_X$ along $\psi$, as in the source. The adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ is the one of Stacks Tag 0096: the composite of the extension/restriction-of-scalars adjunction along $\psi$ (Sheaves, Lemma lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict) and of $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ for modules (Tag 008Z, whose bijection is that of abelian sheaves). The unit of a composite of adjunctions is the composite of the units, and the unit of extension of scalars sends a section $m$ to (the image under sheafification of) $m\otimes1$; hence the unit $\mathcal G\to f_*f^*\mathcal G$ is $s\mapsto\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)\otimes1$, i.e. $f^*s=\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)\otimes1\in(f^*\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$ for $s\in\mathcal G(V)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 6.26 (Tags 0095, 0096: definition of $f^*$ and the adjunction, via Lemmas lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict and 008Z), Section 6.25 (Tag 008X: the $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module $f^{-1}\mathcal G$)

proof.text: *(1) Stalks of $f^{-1}$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk] applied to the abelian sheaf $\mathcal G$ and to the sheaf of rings $\mathcal O_Y$ there are an isomorphism of abelian groups $c_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G_y\to(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$ and a ring isomorphism $c_{\mathcal O}:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to(f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_x$, natural, with $c(s_y)=(\eta_V(s))_x$ on germs. $c_{\mathcal G}$ is semilinear over $c_{\mathcal O}$: for $a_y\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $s_y\in\mathcal G_y$ represented over a common open $V\ni y$, $c_{\mathcal G}(a_ys_y)=c_{\mathcal G}((as)_y)=(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(as))_x=(\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}(a)\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x=(\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}(a))_x(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x=c_{\mathcal O}(a_y)c_{\mathcal G}(s_y)$, using step (0) and that the germ map of a sheaf of modules is compatible with the action (the definition of the $\mathcal O_x$-module structure on a stalk, Sheaves, Lemma lemma-stalk-module).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008H (lemma-stalk-pullback) and Lemma lemma-stalk-module; the proof of Lemma Tag 0098 ('the identification of the stalks of pullback sheaves at $x$ with the corresponding stalks at $f(x)$', Section section-presheaves-structures-functorial)

proof.text: *(2) The ring map.* $\psi_x\circ c_{\mathcal O}=f^\sharp_x:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Indeed, for $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $V\ni y$: $\psi_x(c_{\mathcal O}(a_y))=\psi_x((\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}(a))_x)=(\psi_{f^{-1}V}(\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}(a)))_x=(f^\sharp_V(a))_x=f^\sharp_x(a_y)$, by step (1), the definition of the stalk map of $\psi$, step (0), and the definition of $f^\sharp_x$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] (the germ of $f^\sharp_V(a)$ at $x$); every element of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is such a germ.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 6.26, the paragraph before Lemma Tag 0098 (the stalk maps of an $f$-map and $f^\sharp_x$)

proof.text: *(3) Stalk of the change of rings.* By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-change-of-rings-tensor] applied on $X$ to $\psi:f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ and the $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $\tau:(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x\otimes_{(f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_x}\mathcal O_{X,x}\xrightarrow{\sim}(f^*\mathcal G)_x$ (tensor product along $\psi_x$), natural in $\mathcal G$, with $\tau(m_x\otimes b_x)=(m\otimes b)_x$ for sections $m$ of $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ and $b$ of $\mathcal O_X$ over an open containing $x$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008B (lemma-stalk-tensor-sheaf-modules), as used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0098

proof.text: *(4) Transport along $c$.* The map $\beta:\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x\otimes_{(f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_x}\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $m\otimes b\mapsto c_{\mathcal G}(m)\otimes b$ (left side formed with $f^\sharp_x$, right side with $\psi_x$) is well defined: it is biadditive and balanced, since $c_{\mathcal G}(am)\otimes b=c_{\mathcal O}(a)c_{\mathcal G}(m)\otimes b=c_{\mathcal G}(m)\otimes\psi_x(c_{\mathcal O}(a))b=c_{\mathcal G}(m)\otimes f^\sharp_x(a)b$ by steps (1) and (2). Symmetrically $n\otimes b\mapsto c_{\mathcal G}^{-1}(n)\otimes b$ is well defined (as $c_{\mathcal G}^{-1}$ is semilinear over $c_{\mathcal O}^{-1}$ and $f^\sharp_x\circ c_{\mathcal O}^{-1}=\psi_x$), and the two maps are mutually inverse on generators; $\beta$ is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear. Put $\Phi_{\mathcal G}=(\tau\circ\beta)^{-1}:(f^*\mathcal G)_x\to\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{X,x}$, an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules. This is the identification of Stacks Tag 0098.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules) and its proof (the tensor product on the right uses $f^\sharp_x$)

proof.text: *(5) Germs of $f^*s$.* For $V\ni y$ open and $s\in\mathcal G(V)$: by step (0), $f^*s=\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)\otimes1$ over $f^{-1}V\ni x$, so by step (3) $(f^*s)_x=\tau((\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x\otimes1)$, and by step (1) $(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x=c_{\mathcal G}(s_y)$; hence $(f^*s)_x=\tau(\beta(s_y\otimes1))$, i.e. $\Phi_{\mathcal G}((f^*s)_x)=s_y\otimes1$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 0098: the description of germs follows from the construction of the identification (Tags 008H, 008B, 0096)

proof.text: *(6) Naturality.* For an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$, $f^*u$ is the change of rings of $f^{-1}u$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and $\tau$ is natural in the $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module (step (3)), $c$ is natural in the sheaf (step (1)), and $\beta$ is built from $c$ and the identity of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$; hence $(u_y\otimes1)\circ\Phi_{\mathcal G}=\Phi_{\mathcal G'}\circ(f^*u)_x$. (Alternatively: both sides are $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear and agree on the elements $(f^*s)_x$, $s\in\mathcal G(V)$, by step (5) and $f^*u(f^*s)=f^*(u(s))$ (naturality of the unit); these generate $(f^*\mathcal G)_x$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module since $s_y\otimes1$ generate $\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{X,x}$.)

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 0098 (canonical identification); naturality written out by an agent

proof_origin.place: Sheaves, Lemma 6.26.4 (Tag 0098, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules) and its proof via Lemma Tag 008B and Lemma Tag 008H; the germ formula, the semilinearity of $c_{\mathcal G}$, the identity $\psi_x\circ c=f^\sharp_x$ and naturality are written out by the worker following the constructions of Sections 6.21 and 6.26 (the source says 'see the formulae in Section section-presheaves-structures-functorial')
